units.translation: Thus Weilius for τὰ πολλά [the many things], following Pauw, who conjectured τὰ πολλά παντόφυρτ᾽ ἄγοντ᾽ ἄνευ δίκας [carrying many things all mixed together without justice]. The scholiast explains παντόφυρτα [all mixed together] as παντόθεν συνηγμένα [gathered from all sides].
(thus Porson for ἄξη – φανῇ [you will lead – it will appear]).
where the scholiast says: φελλοὶ τὰ κοῦφα ξύλα τὰ ἀναβαστάζοντα ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ τὰ δίκτυα [corks are the light pieces of wood that buoy up the nets in the sea].
I led the horses, delighting in the reins, under the chariot.
Where are the far-wandering wanderings leading me?
For a woman is leading a man made of beaten gold.
Those who sent me forward led me back again.
Where have you led me?
Where have you led me, wretched as I am, here?
For he (Orpheus) led all things with joy by his voice.
Lead him into the hospitable men's quarters of the house.
Leading this sailor as a suppliant at the hearth of the gods.
So that each of them (the leaders), having obtained his post by lot, might lead his company to the gates.
The multitude he led was a thousand.
Xerxes led them (thus Blomfield for ήγαγεν [led]) — but Xerxes destroyed them.
But now dark-prowed swift ships led them, alas! and ships destroyed them, alas!
And returns from wars led them home without toil and without suffering, prospering.
That he will bring down in time, by force, the one who carries many things all mixed together without justice.
And bringing as a dowry destruction to Ilium.
That he will lead him as a means of overturning his fallen father.
And like the sea, a wave of evils leads.
He orders the spear-bearing attendants to lead.
But you, having roused him with childish barkings, will lead him; and when he is overpowered, he will appear gentler.
And you might lead these willing women.
And one leads another.
And not to lead any of the inhabitants or of the newcomers.
Wishing to lead those who lay hold of the pledges.
And the captured women to be led away.
Being led away by force from the images, in violation of justice.
For the mother's blood leads.
For children are saving voices for a man when he is dead; and like corks they buoy up the net, preserving the spun thread of flax from the deep.
To lead the day of slaughter cheerfully.
I would lead (the gods), if someone does not take these women away.
When you led Hesione, who shared the same father.
He led his dear wife.
But come, Persians, let us take counsel.
Come now, king, how shall I address you?
Come now, let us also begin the dance.
Come now, let us speak good prayers; come.
Come, release the blood of deeds done long ago.
